additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: ID0420344-DC/Si-D/DE-[ MP / N8 160373321 ]  Charging point 1 (left) out of service CRM:02684000143
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Frau Menne,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0420344.
I apologize for the delayed answer due to the holiday period.
The charger was suffering from severe communication issues between the internal controllers, resulting in the so-called “error polling coap”, which was temporarily setting the outlet DC1 out of order:
I performed the following corrective actions:
As per my previous email, the charger was running on an unstable FW version v5.0.21. On 28.04.2025 I updated the FW version to v6.0.3.
On 29.04.2025, I installed a Hotfix v1.4.11 on the EcoG controller. The Hotfix includes hardening patches regarding CoAP communication and Modbus reconnection hardening. This Hotfix is meant to solve such communication issues.
Since the Hotfix installation, I did not notice any further unavailability of outlet DC1. Could you please confirm that the charger is not suffering anymore of unavailability of DC1?
Looking forward to hearing your feedback soon.
W

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: AW: AW: ID0420344-DC/Si-D/DE-[ MP / N8 160373321 ]  Charging point 1 (left) out of service CRM:02684000143
additional_info.body:
Good evening Frau Menne,
I had the time to deeply analyze both the unavailability of outlet DC1 and the failed sessions on outlet DC2. Here is for you a detailed overview:
Outlet DC2:
Yesterday morning (12.05.2025) happened #2 events of charging session interrupted on DC2, both with the same EV (EVMAC:
00.18.23.bd.c4.17)
Both charging sessions stopped due to
DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101 ('VIV:0 PLE:1 KON:1'), where:
VIV:0 → in case of an invalid sensor reading
PLE:1→ in case of an plausibility error (temperature difference between +/- 15 deg C too high)
KON:1: → in case the contact temperature sensors are not okay
I had a screening of this error over the past month, and it happened only #1 other time on 30.04.2025, also with the same EV as before.
I would suggest, as first steps:
to remove the “Boost mode” setting from SCB and check if this issue will happen again in the future.
to have a visual inspection of DC2 plug and clean it in case of dirt.
Only if several charging sessions are getting interrupted due to
DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101, then it is recommended to replace the cable.
Outlet DC1:
I analyzed the last 2 events of outlet DC1 being Out of order reported by you. I could not find a clear root-cause, beside seeing some communication issue between the SECC_LE and the PLC.
My suggestion would be to check the Ethernet cable for communication issue between EcoG_LE and PLC, and in case these communication issues still happen, to replace the EcoG_LE.
A reboot of the  charger proved to solve temporarily the unavailable state.
Please report here in the ticket if any further unavaiilability of outlet DC1 appears, so that we can investigate further and possibly find a clearer root-cause.
I am including in this loop @Lukas Berger, who is coordinator for chargers in region Germany for visibility.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you.
W

additional_info.subject: Handover from ES to NOC
additional_info.body:
Problem Description
: DC2 Temp cable sensor and DC1 unavailable
Suspected Root Cause
: For DC2, only #2 events with a single vehicle. Informed region to monitor charger and plug.
For DC1, installed Hotfix v1.4.11 upon v6.1.3 and again upon v7.0.5
Action Performed (ES)
: Logs analysis, FW upgrade and x2 Hotfix installation
Charger SW Version
: v7.0.5+v1.4.11
Reason for Handover (ES/NOC
): As per agreed with RC-DE service coordinator, Hotfix installed and ticket to be closed. Please close the ticket
